stories.title: Man fined after 700 frozen and taxidermied animals found on Victorian property
summary: Antiques store owner, 74, pleads guilty to 13 charges after regulator uncovers hundreds of animals at his home and shopGet our new political email, free app or daily news podcastThe white-walled room packed with magpies, galahs and sulphur-crested cockatoos, foxes and possums is eerily quiet.

As a video pans across shelves filled with these and many other species, there is no flapping or squawking or hissing; the animals are frozen and silent.They are among the more than 700 native animals that were found illegally taxidermied and frozen that were seized from the property of a Victorian antiques store owner last year.

stories.title: Canadian publisher Boréal ends relationship with novelist Thélyson Orélien over alleged use of AI
summary: Author withdrawn from France’s Prix Goncourt last month has repeatedly denied using artificial intelligence to write novelThe publisher of top-selling Haitian Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien, who was removed from France’s most prestigious literary prize list last month, has confirmed the author used artificial intelligence to help write his novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was Either That or Die).Orélien has denied allegations that he used AI on his breakthrough novel and, last week, Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal said it was standing by the 38-year-old writer.
